doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bookie's studio, bands and downtown clubs
title: Discovering Roy Hargrove in Texas
summary: Cobb tells how he and Larry Clothier found Roy Hargrove in high school.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Nat, Larry Willis. Those was the home guys. I think he went in partnership with Ragman. You know Ragman?

They were in partnership a little bit, making records. We went down to Texas and got Roy Hargrove. Larry’s his manager still. We got him when he was down there in high school. There was a place that we played called Dreams. The club was named something Dreams and something [Caravan of Dreams]. That was the club that they played down that way. He was still in high school, like I just said. His mother and daddy
used to bring him to the little gigs that he had down there. He got out, came to New York, and he’s doing what he’s doing now. He’s a talented little guy from a long time ago.
